current_difficulty_reason: The usual finite-index-subgroup counting argument fails when the infinite normal subgroup is not finitely generated. The authors use the locally finite Cayley-Abels graph to construct a finite-index subgroup as a finite-ball stabilizer and prove that its fibers are invariant under the whole lattice. This new normalization construction then lets discrete normalizers force the two ambient lattices to be commensurable, beyond the classical rigidity and normalizer prerequisites alone.
